name: Homemade Carr's-Style Whole Wheat Crackers

ingredients.name: finely ground whole wheat flour, plus more for dusting
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/4-inch cubes

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 180°C (350°F). Combine whole wheat flour, sugar, wheat germ, salt, cream of tartar, baking powder, and baking soda in the bowl of a food processor and pulse to combine. Add butter and process until the mix looks floury and fine, with no visible chunks of butter, then add buttermilk and pulse only until the dough comes together in a ball.

Transfer dough to a lightly floured surface and, using as much flour as needed along the way, roll until just shy of 0.5 cm thick. Dust off excess flour with a pastry brush and loosen dough from counter with an offset spatula. Create steam vents with a fork, bamboo skewer, or docking tool, then cut dough into 2 1/4–inch rounds and transfer to parchment-lined half sheet pans. Gather up scraps, knead, roll, dock, and cut as before.

Bake crackers until firm to the touch and pale gold around the edges, about 25 minutes. Cool directly on baking sheets and serve at room temperature (the crackers will not be crisp while warm). Store leftovers in an airtight container up to 1 month at room temperature.

description: Thick, tender, hearty, and buttery, these whole grain crackers have that same touch of sweetness from the original Carr's, making them a perfect match for rich and savory accompaniments, like peanut butter or cheese.
notes:
Optional substitutions: cultured lowfat buttermilk → kefir

Notes: If buttermilk's hard to come by where you live, plain kefir works well, but avoid common buttermilk substitutions, like a combination of milk and lemon juice, which won't taste or behave the same way in this dough.
author: Stella Parks
